source.title: The Same But Different: Structural Similarities and Differences in Multilingual Language Modeling
source.authors: Ruochen Zhang; Qinan Yu; Matianyu Zang; Carsten Eickhoff; Ellie Pavlick

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study applies path patching and IOI head-function analyses, following the original IOI work, to additional models and languages. It also uses information-flow routes to examine component overlap.
record.gate_note: The paper reports IOI accuracy and zero-rank rates, but those behavioral scores alone do not establish the circuit properties in the claim versions. It also summarizes earlier IOI findings from Wang et al.; those cited results are not recorded as this study's results.
record.test_reason: The study runs Wang et al.-style path patching and head-function checks on IOI in new settings: BLOOM-560M in English and Chinese, and Chinese CPM-Generate-distill. It compares the head classes and roles it finds with the original circuit and reproduces the GPT2-small circuit qualitatively. The main contribution is new models and languages, so T3 fits better than T1.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also conclude that, for past-tense morphology, multilingual Qwen reuses shared copy heads but adds English-specific past-tense heads and late FFNs. That result concerns a different task, not IOI.
record.recipe_differences: Uses path patching and IOI head-function metrics in the style of the original, with information-flow routes added; it does not report the original faithfulness, completeness, and minimality evaluation.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper says path-patching circuits depend strongly on minimal-pair template design and that information-flow routes tend to identify more generic components and larger circuits. It does not report IOI outcome changes across alternative prompt distributions.
record.problems: The cross-language activation-frequency analysis uses 50 examples per language. The paper reports no uncertainty estimates for the IOI circuit comparisons. It notes that path-patching results depend on minimal-pair design and that the findings are limited to specific tasks and datasets.
record.rows_left_out: No IOI benchmark accuracy or zero-rank rows were retained because those scores establish task performance, not the circuit properties named by the versions. No other IOI circuit outcomes were omitted.

untested.parts: Exact count of 26 heads and 7 classes; faithfulness, completeness and minimality criteria.
All of it: no ablation of name movers to look for backup heads.
Other sizes and training checkpoints; reuse of IOI components for other tasks.
Alternative ablation types and metrics; quantitative comparison of circuits recovered by different methods.
All of it: no test of how faithfulness or completeness depends on ablation, metric or prompt distribution.
No circuit comparison across name orders, templates or more names. Flipped-order results are accuracy only.

missing.what: CPM head identities and roles: name movers 8.9 and 9.10 copy IO, 11.7 copies both IO and S, and copy suppression head 11.2 suppresses S.
Validation of Duplicate Token, Previous Token and Induction Heads by attention scores on random token sequences, in BLOOM English and Chinese.

record.verdict_notes: No uncertainty estimates are given. The cross-language overlap uses 50 examples per language. The remark that path-patching circuits depend on minimal-pair design is a general methodological comment, not a V5 test. The r2 limits_scope label was dropped because it is a control and cannot show reuse.

versions.untested_parts: The study analyzes GPT2-small's IOI circuit and reports that it resembles the previously described circuit, but does not establish the exact count of 26 heads, seven classes, or the original faithfulness, completeness, and minimality criteria.
It does not ablate the main name-mover heads to test whether backup heads take over.

The study tests circuits across English and Chinese and across several models, but not multiple sizes or training checkpoints. It does not establish broad component reuse across other tasks; its past-tense comparison is an activation-overlap control, not a direct test of reuse.
It reports converging results from path patching and information-flow routes, but does not systematically compare alternative ablation types or a range of metrics for recovering the same circuit.

The paper notes general method limitations but does not test how IOI circuit faithfulness or completeness changes with ablation choice, metric, or prompt distribution, nor how much of IOI behavior the circuit explains.
The paper uses multiple templates and reports normal/flipped IOI performance, but does not compare circuit components across name orders, templates, or prompts with more names.

rows.subject: BLOOM-560M
rows.operation_detail: Compared information-flow-route head activation frequencies across English and Chinese IOI examples.
rows.measure: Pearson correlation of head activation frequencies
rows.note: The authors describe high cross-language overlap in important heads.
rows.check: Remove V4. This is one method (information flow routes) applied across languages, not a comparison between methods. The comparison point is the past-tense control (ρ=0.48), not 'not stated'. It measures head overlap, not head roles.

source_check.correct: English–Chinese IOI head-activation-frequency correlation: ρ=0.72. Comparison control, English IOI versus English past-tense task: ρ=0.48.

rows.subject: BLOOM-560M
rows.operation_detail: Compared information-flow-route head activation frequencies for IOI and the past-tense control task.

conditions.value: English IOI vs English past tense

rows.measure: Pearson correlation of head activation frequencies
rows.note: The authors say the control uses significantly different heads from the cross-language IOI comparison, while also noting anecdotal overlap in some generically important heads.
rows.check: This is the study's control for the cross-language comparison, not a test of IOI component reuse. A 0.48 activation-frequency correlation, with anecdotal overlap of 'generic' heads, cannot show whether IOI roles are reused in the past-tense task.

rows.subject: BLOOM-560M
rows.operation_detail: Used path patching to identify IOI components and Wang et al.-style metrics to validate their functions for English inputs.
rows.measure: Identified circuit components and their stated functions
rows.value: The identified functionalities align with those in Wang et al. (2023); path-patching and functional analyses are described as highly similar across the two experiments.
rows.note: The paper does not provide a full enumerated head count in the text.
rows.check: Remove V1 (V1 concerns GPT-2 small only) and V4 (path patching is the original method, not an alternative one). BLOOM English functions align with Wang et al.

rows.subject: BLOOM-560M
rows.operation_detail: Used path patching to identify IOI components and Wang et al.-style metrics to validate their functions for Chinese inputs.
rows.measure: Cross-language circuit overlap and identified head functions
rows.value: The authors report highly similar English and Chinese circuits, with shared components performing the same functionalities.
rows.note: The study states that path patching and functional validation yield highly similar results.
rows.check: Remove V4. This uses the same path-patching method; it is a cross-language comparison within BLOOM.

source_check.locator_found: §3.4 and Figure 2 caption; Appendix B.1 and Figures 6–7.

rows.subject: GPT2-small
rows.operation_detail: Applied path patching to identify and inspect the English IOI circuit.
rows.value: The authors report a circuit similar to Wang et al. (2023), including Negative Name Mover heads.
rows.note: This bears on the reported circuit and roles, but not on the original numerical or faithfulness/completeness/minimality criteria.
rows.check: Remove V3, since GPT2-small is the original model. The reproduction is qualitative only (similar circuit, Negative Name Movers present), with no head count or faithfulness/completeness/minimality checks.

rows.subject: CPM-Generate-distill
rows.size_stated: Same architecture and number of parameters as GPT2-small; no separate parameter count stated
rows.operation_detail: Applied path patching to identify and inspect the Chinese IOI circuit.
rows.value: The authors report a largely similar circuit, but no Negative Name Mover heads; a Copy Suppression Head was found instead.
rows.note: The authors describe the Copy Suppression Head as suppressing the repeated name through a route different from the Negative Name Mover pattern.
rows.check: Largely similar circuit, but no Negative Name Movers; a Copy Suppression Head (11.2) reads from Duplicate Token Heads instead. Name mover 11.7 copies both IO and S.

rows.subject: CPM-Generate-distill
rows.size_stated: Same architecture and number of parameters as GPT2-small; no separate parameter count stated
rows.operation_detail: Ablated S-inhibition head 7.0 and inspected the original name-mover heads.
rows.measure: Name-mover preference for IO versus repeated subject names
rows.value: After ablation, the original name movers stop preferring IO tokens and promote both IO and subject tokens.
rows.note: This supports the reported functional role of the S-inhibition head; it is not a test of backup name-mover heads.
rows.check: Correct as recorded. It confirms the S-inhibition role of head 7.0 in CPM.

rows.subject: BLOOM-560M
rows.operation_detail: Compared findings from information-flow routes with path-patching and functional analyses.
rows.measure: Agreement between analysis methods on the primary circuit findings
rows.value: The authors state that the methods produce results consistent with the primary claims; their identified components and functions are described as highly similar.
rows.note: This is a qualitative convergence report, not a systematic comparison of ablation types or all circuit metrics.
rows.check: Qualitative agreement only. The authors also say information flow routes find 'more generic components and larger circuits' and resolve importance only every two layers. No quantitative overlap between the methods is reported.
